source.title: On Privileged and Convergent Bases in Neural Network Representations
source.authors: Davis Brown; Nikhil Vyas; Yamini Bansal

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly measures alignment between independently initialized networks and reports that basis correlation does not rise with width, while showing that shared frozen early layers can increase alignment.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports random-rotation experiments and linear-mode-connectivity results. Rotation recovery and noise-robustness results do not directly measure any listed convergence version, so they are summarized under fits_no_version. The paper cites prior results about perm-LMC barriers; those cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures neuron-basis alignment (perm-corr) between ResNet20 networks trained from different seeds across widths 1x–32x. It reports that alignment stays nearly constant and below a random-network baseline, while LMC barriers fall with width. These results bear on V3 (unit-level caveat), V6 (measure dependence), V7 (incomplete, flat alignment) and, narrowly, V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that LMC overstates neuron similarity across runs, since its improvement with width is partly due to noise robustness. Networks do not converge to a unique basis even at high width, yet the basis is privileged because rotations cannot be inverted. Freezing a few early layers identically gives a cheap route to a convergent basis.
record.recipe_differences: Uses permutation-correlation, linear mode connectivity, rotational interventions, and identity stitching rather than the original sources' representation-similarity measurements; focuses on neural-network bases, width, and shared frozen layers.
record.method_sensitivity: Width affects linear mode connectivity and identity-stitching success but not perm-corr as reported; freezing early layers increases perm-corr and lowers identity-stitching penalty. The residual-stream modification has largely comparable results.

fits_no_version.finding: Freezing a model's first l blocks into a second model raises perm-corr in the later, retrained blocks and lowers the identity-stitching penalty. Two frozen blocks are enough. This holds for ConvNeXt on CIFAR-10, ViT on ImageNet and ResNet-20, and does not depend on a linear residual stream.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharing early layers fixes the basis that the downstream layers learn across training runs.

fits_no_version.finding: A random rotation of Myrtle-CNN pre-activations cannot be undone by retraining the later layers. The resulting error approaches that of random features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nonlinear network layers have a privileged basis that is not rotation-invariant.

fits_no_version.finding: The LMC barrier without permutation, and the accuracy drop from averaging a trained network with a random one, both shrink with width.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width improves LMC through robustness to noise, not through basis similarity.

record.problems: Most plotted outcomes have no extractable numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The width sweep is for Resnet20 and does not establish scaling with capability or across diverse architectures, objectives, data, or modalities. Several positive alignment results use an explicit shared-layer intervention.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-layer plotted values and each individual frozen-prefix curve in Sections 5 and Appendix A (Figures 3–7) are not separately extracted; the rows record the paper's textual summaries because the plots do not provide readable numerical values. Figure 2's layer-by-layer rotation and random-feature error values are also not rowed because they do not directly measure a listed version.

untested.parts: Different architectures, objectives, data or modalities. Kernel or representational-similarity measures rather than a neuron-basis measure. Capability beyond width.
Whether shared features or subspaces exist despite unaligned units (no CCA/CKA or subspace measure).
Entire version for independently trained models: no learned linear map, stitching without shared layers, relative representations or unpaired mapping.
Similarity-measure hyperparameters such as number of neighbours, choice of input data, out-of-distribution inputs.
Whether shared data or objectives explain alignment.

missing.what: Perm-LMC barrier vs width as a separate row (falls with width), measured alongside perm-corr
LMC barrier without permutation, and accuracy drop for a noisy (trained plus random) network, both falling with width

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V3 'challenges' label is replaced: V3 already concedes that individual units differ, so unit-level non-convergence limits rather than refutes it. The reader's V6 'challenges' label is inverted: V6 is itself a challenge claim, and measure-dependent results support it. All shared-frozen-layer rows are intervention results, not convergence between independent models. No values can be read from the figures.

versions.untested_parts: Tests width scaling for ResNet20, but not broader differences in architecture, objective, data, modality, capability, or performance.
No paired image-caption vision-language representations are tested.
Measures neuron-basis permutation correlation, not shared features or subspaces generally; does not test whether individual units differ while subspaces agree.

Tests identity stitching under shared early layers, not learned linear maps, relative representations, stitching across independently trained full models without shared layers, or unpaired-data mapping.
Does not identify or compare recurring interpretable features or circuits.
Compares permutation correlation with linear mode connectivity in the reported width sweep; does not vary similarity-measure settings such as neighbour count or test out-of-distribution inputs.
Shows results for same-architecture models and an intervention sharing early layers; does not isolate the effects of shared training data or objectives against a common-reality explanation.

rows.subject: Resnet20
rows.size_stated: Width multipliers 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, and 32; widest model is Resnet20-32x.
rows.stage_stated: Networks trained with SGD; independent initializations and batch orderings.
rows.operation_detail: Measured permutation-correlation between independently trained networks across width.
rows.value: Figure only; described as almost constant with width.
rows.note: The paper says perm-corr does not improve with width, despite the decline in the perm-LMC barrier.
rows.check: State is per version. V1: absent, since perm-corr does not rise with width. V3: partial, since unit matching is incomplete, which V3 itself allows. V6: observed, since perm-LMC barrier falls while perm-corr stays flat. V7: observed, since the text says perm-corr is very far from 1 at all tested widths. The row also merges perm-corr with the perm-LMC barrier; the barrier should be its own row.
